stories.title: Kidder Mathews Expanding into Dallas
stories.excerpt: Kidder Mathews is expanding into Dallas, Texas, with the addition of six brokers. Mart Martindale, Brandon Beeson, Wilson Stafford, John David Cobb, and Claire Schmeltekopf form an investment sales team, while Barrett Jones joins as a healthcare tenant advisory specialist. The move marks the firm’s first entry into Texas and expands its footprint to 20 offices across six states. “Dallas has long been one of the country’s most dynamic commercial real estate markets, and we have been deliberate about finding the right people before planting our flag,” said Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Bill Frame, SIOR, CCIM. The new office will serve the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex and be led by former Edge Capital Markets co-founders Mart Martindale, Brandon Beeson, and Wilson Stafford. The brokers built a platform within Edge Realty Partners serving both institutional and private clients throughout Texas and surrounding states. Kidder Mathews plans to add Asset Services and Valuation Advisory teams, extending beyond brokerage in Dallas-Fort Worth. The post Kidder Mathews Expanding into Dallas appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Kidder Mathews enters Dallas-Fort Worth with 6 brokers; first Texas office.
Former Edge Capital Markets co-founders lead investment sales team.
Firm plans Asset Services and Valuation Advisory expansion beyond brokerage.
stories.summary: Kidder Mathews, a major CRE brokerage, has opened its first Texas office in Dallas-Fort Worth by hiring six brokers, including three co-founders from Edge Capital Markets who built a regional institutional and private client platform. The move expands Kidder Mathews to 20 offices across six states and signals intent to add Asset Services and Valuation Advisory capabilities in the DFW metro.
stories.impact: Brokerage expansion into DFW reflects confidence in the market's activity and liquidity, but has minimal direct bearing on multifamily demand or supply. More relevant as market intelligence: the firm's focus on institutional clients and valuation advisory may improve capital formation and deal flow visibility for large developers already active there.

stories.title: Zar Properties Buys NoHo’s 31-35 Great Jones Street for $21M
stories.excerpt: Zar Properties has bought two NoHo mixed-use buildings at 31-35 Great Jones Street for $21 million, Commercial Observer has learned. The nearly identical adjacent buildings between Lafayette Street and the Bowery have been owned by the Scott family of Great Jones St. Realty for the last five decades, at least. The family is selling at a time when office, retail and residential have become more competitive in the area. Albert Sultan and Joseph Kassin of Kassin Sabbagh Realty, known simply as KSR, represented the seller in the transaction. The two commercial properties — one seven-story property and an adjacent three-story, late-19th-century building — were only on the market for about two months with competing offers until the sellers settled on a cash offer from Zar, according to Sultan. “With all the AI and tech tenants that are propping up the market in terms of leasing, the companies want to be centered around Downtown and live-work-play submarkets like SoHo and NoHo,” Sultan told CO. “I think that is a testament to why this building had as much interest; we had three or four buyers all competing for this.” But Zar did not waste any time, closing the deal within 30 days. Current tenants at the NoHo properties include art gallery Aicon Contemporary. Just across the street at 375 Lafayette Street, Minskoff Equities and Edison Properties are constructing two 99-unit multifamily properties where a parking lot currently sits. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Zar Properties buys 31-35 Great Jones Street NoHo for $21M in cash.
Two mixed-use buildings sold after 5 decades of Scott family ownership.
AI and tech tenants driving leasing competition in SoHo/NoHo submarkets.
stories.summary: Zar Properties acquired a pair of NoHo mixed-use buildings (7-story and 3-story) for $21 million in cash after only two months on market with competing offers. The transaction reflects strength in Downtown Manhattan's live-work-play submarkets, driven by clustering of AI and tech companies seeking central locations near residential and retail amenities.
stories.impact: Tech job concentration (AI especially) is fueling office and mixed-use leasing in lower Manhattan submarkets, which signals sustained demand pressure on residential nearby; however, this story focuses on office/retail conversion. For multifamily developers, the play is whether NoHo/SoHo's tech talent influx and density justify new or converted apartment supply, or if existing stock absorbs demand.

stories.title: MNRK Music Group Inks 8K SF at Rosen’s 443 Park Avenue South
stories.excerpt: Independent music company MNRK Music Group has leased 7,629 square feet at the Rosen family’s 443 Park Avenue South office building, Commercial Observer has learned. The seven-year, seven-month office lease occupies the entire ninth floor of the 11-story tower, according to Koeppel Rosen, the leasing and management agent for the Rosen family portfolio. The building is at the corner of Park Avenue and East 30th Street near Manhattan’s Murray Hill neighborhood. Koeppel Rosen’s Max Koeppel handled the deal in-house for the landlord. Transwestern’s Luke Dillmeier, Patrick Heeg and Thomas Hines negotiated on behalf of MNRK Music in the transaction. The asking rent was $48 per square foot, according to a source familiar with the deal. MNRK Music, which manages a portfolio of labels and acts that includes Last Gang Records and folk band The Lumineers, currently lists its New York offices at the Trump Organization’s 40 Wall Street. The group moved into 443 Park Avenue South in mid-July, according to a source. It is unclear whether the move marks a relocation or an expansion for MNRK Music. Other tenants at the Midtown South building include cloud data firm Ardoq, software firm LMI and architecture firm David Smotrich & Partners. Its retail component is occupied by a Joe Coffee Company location, as well as a storefront for apparel and footwear retailer Comme Des Garcons. Spokespeople for MNRK Music Group and Transwestern did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: MNRK Music Group leases 7,629 SF at 443 Park Avenue South, 9th floor.
Seven-year lease at $48/SF; moved from Trump Organization's 40 Wall Street.
Relocation or expansion status unclear; mid-July occupancy.
stories.summary: Independent music company MNRK Music Group leased the entire ninth floor (7,629 SF) of 443 Park Avenue South in Murray Hill for seven years and seven months at $48/SF asking rent, relocating from 40 Wall Street. The deal closed by mid-July but it remains unclear if this is a net expansion or internal relocation.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Office lease activity in Murray Hill and Park Avenue South does not materially signal residential demand shifts; music/entertainment company relocations are typically too small to drive neighborhood population or housing demand growth.

stories.title: ESRT’s 1359 Broadway Selling to Thor for $218M
stories.excerpt: Only a month after Commercial Observer learned it was going on the market, Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT) has found a buyer for 1359 Broadway in Thor Equities, which agreed to pay $218 million for the 22-story office building, according to sources. This is not much lower than the $225 million the 486,000-square-foot property was being shopped around for earlier this summer. Neither ESRT nor Thor responded to CO’s requests for comment. ESRT was represented by Newmark’s Adam Spies, Josh King, Adam Doneger, Avery Silverstein, Marcella Fasulo and Doug Harmon, who also did not respond to requests for comment by press time. CO was not able to learn who represented Thor. The property, just two blocks north of Herald Square, was 95 percent occupied as of last month, having inked recent leases with Infinium Wall Systems, SLCE Architects and nonprofit Braven, and has a Wolfgang’s Steakhouse and Wokuni in the retail portion. The purchase, expected to close in the next month or two and not official yet, is not Thor’s first dip into the Midtown office market this year. In March, CO reported that Joe Sitt’s company had purchased Michael Haddad’s 58,000-square-foot office and retail building, 1165 Broadway, for $56 million. Max Gross can be reached at mgross@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Empire State Realty Trust sells 1359 Broadway to Thor Equities for $218M.
22-story, 486K SF office tower; 95% occupied; two blocks north Herald Square.
Property on market ~1 month; price ~$7M below asking ($225M).
stories.summary: ESRT divested 1359 Broadway, a 22-story, 486,000-SF office tower near Herald Square, to Thor Equities for $218 million after roughly one month on market. The property was 95% leased with recent tenants including Infinium Wall Systems, SLCE Architects, and nonprofit Braven, plus retail (Wolfgang's Steakhouse, Wokuni).
stories.impact: Sale price ~3% below ask suggests moderate softness in Manhattan office investment, but the quick close and high occupancy imply stable leasing. For multifamily: this is near Macy's/Herald Square, a dense retail corridor with limited residential new supply; existing apartments benefit from stable office employment and foot traffic, but no new residential signal here.

stories.title: Finmarc Buys NoVA Office Complex for $78M
stories.excerpt: Finmarc Management has acquired a pair of office towers in Tysons, Va., for $77.5 million as the company begins another wave of acquisitions while doubling down on office space in Northern Virginia. The Bethesda, Md.-based investment firm acquired Highline at Greensboro from CIM Group. The two 10-story Class A buildings at 8401 and 8405 Greensboro Drive total roughly 460,000 square feet and were 70 percent leased at the time of the sale. “We remain buyers of office buildings and other assets in the greater DMV market, especially Northern Virginia because of our continued confidence in the regional market fundamentals,” Finmarc Principal Neil Markus said in a statement. Highline at Greensboro is near The Boro mixed-use complex and the Greensboro Metro station. The property features a fitness center, a golf simulator and a day care. Over the past two years, new tenants Mortgage One Solutions signed for 23,108 square feet and Tegna took 23,016 square feet. Cushman & Wakefield’s Paul Collins and Kevin Sidney represented CIM. Metropolis Capital Advisors’ Cliff Mendelson assisted Finmarc with the debt placement. Cushman & Wakefield’s Josh Masi and Paige Barger handle leasing at the Highline at Greensboro. Finmarc has been betting on discounted Northern Virginia offices. The company paid $51 million late last year for the nearly 620,000-square-foot Dulles Corner portfolio after acquiring the roughly 500,000-square-foot Trinity Centre for nearly $40 million the previous summer. The company funded the Highline acquisition partly with proceeds from three dispositions completed over the past six weeks, including office/flex and retail assets in Virginia and North Carolina. Finmarc also said it has more dry powder coming from expected sales over the next two to three months, and plans to reinvest the proceeds into another $250 million to $300 million of acquisitions. The firm currently owns and manages nearly 7.5 million square feet across the Mid-Atlantic. Gregory Corn
bullets: Finmarc acquires Highline at Greensboro, Tysons, VA for $77.5M from CIM.
Two 10-story Class A buildings; 460K SF; 70% leased; near metro station.
New tenants: Mortgage One (23K SF), Tegna (23K SF) in past 2 years.
stories.summary: Finmarc Management acquired a pair of Class A office towers (460,000 SF total) in Tysons Corner, Northern Virginia for $77.5 million from CIM Group. The property was 70% leased and features recent tenant additions (Mortgage One Solutions, Tegna) and amenities (fitness center, golf simulator, day care). Finmarc stated continued confidence in regional DMV fundamentals.
stories.impact: Finmarc's continued office acquisitions in NoVA signal investor confidence in the submarket despite national office headwinds, suggesting stable corporate employment and office demand. For multifamily: Tysons near the Greensboro Metro is a commuter shed; continued office leasing supports residential demand in surrounding submarkets, though the Boro mixed-use development may cannibalize standalone multifamily. Monitor whether leasing velocity holds.

stories.title: L3 Capital Secures 24K SF for Bylt Basics, Zara Flagships in Williamsburg
stories.excerpt: L3 Capital’s 108 North Sixth Street and 184-192 Bedford Avenue are welcoming two retail flagships to Williamsburg, Brooklyn. Men’s apparel brand Bylt Basics has selected 108 North Sixth Street, between Berry Street and Wythe Avenue, to host its first permanent New York City storefront, Commercial Observer has learned, in a bold signal of the retail corridor’s growing retail dominance. Fast fashion retailer Zara also plans to set up shop at L3’s nearby development down the block, 184-192 Bedford Avenue, according to a source familiar with the deals. Bylt signed on for 2,085 square feet at 108 North Sixth Street, and Zara’s new digs at 184-192 Bedford Avenue will span 22,060 square feet across three floors, according to the source. Zara will join current tenant Intuit TurboTax at the Bedford Avenue development. The Real Deal first reported the Zara lease. Spokespeople for Bylt and Zara did not immediately respond to requests for comment. L3 Capital was represented in both deals by a Newmark team of Ariel Schuster, Tyler King and Michael Paster, while MCD Retail’s Mitchell Dearman negotiated on behalf of Zara and Bylt. Spokespeople for L3 Capital, Newmark and MCD Retail did not respond to requests for comment. The asking rent for Bylt’s long-term lease was not disclosed, but retail rents inside nearby 184 Bedford Avenue vary from roughly $550 per square foot on the ground floor to $150 per square foot on the second floor. L3 Capital, a Chicago-based private equity firm, completed the redevelopment of 184-192 Bedford Avenue last year. The vacant, adjacent buildings that previously occupied the lots were demolished in 2022. L3 followed a similar playbook at 108-112 North Sixth Street, where it redeveloped three separate lots into a two-story commercial building in 2024. bullets: Bylt Basics opens first NYC flagship (2,085 SF) at 108 North Sixth, Williamsburg.
Zara leases 22,060 SF across 3 floors at 184-192 Bedford Avenue.
L3 Capital properties anchored by major retail brands signaling corridor strength.
stories.summary: Men's apparel brand Bylt Basics and fast-fashion retailer Zara signed flagship leases at L3 Capital properties in Williamsburg, Brooklyn—Bylt at 108 North Sixth (2,085 SF) and Zara at 184-192 Bedford (22,060 SF across three floors). Both deals underscore the neighborhood's emerging retail dominance and appeal to major consumer brands.
stories.impact: Heavy retail anchor leasing in Williamsburg signals strong foot traffic, daytime density, and consumer spend—drivers of renter appeal. For multifamily: this validates Williamsburg as a live-work-play destination, supporting existing residential values and justifying new supply. However, Williamsburg is already densely built; the real signal is whether retail success translates to in-migration and ability to sustain higher rent growth, particularly in adjacent, less-developed adjacent pockets.

stories.title: Nicola Offloads 143K-SF Chandler Business Park
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield’s National Industrial Advisory Group arranged the sale of South Valley Business Park. The industrial assets total 143,813 square feet across two Class A buildings located at 1710 and 1720 East Germann Road in Chandler, Arizona. The buildings were originally developed in 2022 as a joint venture between Hopewell Development and Nicola Wealth Real Estate (NWRE), and were subsequently acquired by Nicola Wealth as an investment property later that same year. Cushman & Wakefield’s Will Strong, Jack Stamets, Molly Miller, Michael Matchett and Madeline Warren facilitated the transaction, representing both the seller and the undisclosed buyer.South Valley Business Park is fully leased to five tenants and benefits from modern industrial specifications designed to accommodate a wide range of manufacturing, distribution, and logistics users. EMD Electronics is a long-term tenant at the location. The property’s direct frontage along East Germann Road and immediate access to Loop 202 provide convenient connectivity to the greater Phoenix freeway network. The post Nicola Offloads 143K-SF Chandler Business Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Nicola Wealth offloads South Valley Business Park, Chandler, AZ; 143.8K SF.
Two Class A buildings built 2022, fully leased to 5 tenants.
Buyer undisclosed; property has East Germann Road frontage and Loop 202 access.
stories.summary: Nicola Wealth divested South Valley Business Park in Chandler, Arizona—two Class A industrial buildings (143,813 SF total) developed in 2022 as a joint venture, subsequently held as investment property. The fully leased facility features direct freeway access and houses industrial/manufacturing/logistics tenants including long-term anchor EMD Electronics.
stories.impact: Industrial asset sale in Chandler reflects investor reallocation but does not directly impact multifamily supply or demand. Chandler is growing, but this transaction alone does not signal employment or population influx. Monitor Chandler's broader industrial absorption and employment trends; strong logistics/manufacturing activity could eventually drive worker migration and multifamily demand.

stories.title: Creation, Crow Holdings Building 700K-SF Avondale Warehouse Facility
stories.excerpt: Creation in partnership with a real estate fund advised by Crow Holdings Capital, has begun construction on Avondale Tech Center, a three-building Class-A industrial campus spanning 38 acres and totaling approximately 700,000 square feet. The three buildings range from 212,184 to 254,264 square feet and feature 36-foot clear heights. The development will include tenant-focused outdoor amenities not typically found in industrial developments, such as dedicated gathering areas for each building, a walking path encircling the campus and shared pickleball courts. The campus is designed to serve advanced manufacturing, research and development and assembly operations, with target industries including pharmaceutical development, aerospace, semiconductor manufacturing and defense contracting. LGE Design Build is both the architect and general contractor for the project. Leading leasing efforts are Riley Gilbert along with John Lydon and Kelly Royle of JLL. Completion is targeted for Q3 2027. The post Creation, Crow Holdings Building 700K-SF Avondale Warehouse Facility appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Creation and Crow Holdings Capital building Avondale Tech Center, Phoenix, AZ.
700K SF across 3 buildings, 38 acres, 36-ft clear heights; Q3 2027 delivery.
Target tenants: pharma, aerospace, semiconductor, defense; tenant amenities include pickleball courts.
stories.summary: Creation and Crow Holdings Capital have begun construction on Avondale Tech Center, a 38-acre, 700,000-SF industrial campus near Phoenix targeting advanced manufacturing, R&D, and assembly operations in pharma, aerospace, semiconductor, and defense. The three Class A buildings (212K–254K SF each) feature 36-foot clear heights and unusual tenant amenities (walking path, pickleball courts). Delivery is targeted for Q3 2027.
stories.impact: Large, specialized industrial pipeline serving high-wage, stable sectors (aerospace, defense, pharma, semiconductors) signals employer clustering and job growth in the Phoenix metro. Avondale is west of central Phoenix; if leasing succeeds and clusters develop, could drive significant worker in-migration to western Phoenix suburbs, strengthening multifamily demand in Avondale, Goodyear, and adjacent submarkets. Monitor pre-leasing and tenant announcements closely.

stories.title: CBRE: U.S. and Canadian AI Jobs Grow 45% Year-Over-Year
stories.excerpt: The ranks of U.S. and Canadian tech talent skilled in artificial intelligence grew by 45% in the past year, with AI-related roles now accounting for nearly a third of U.S. tech-talent job listings and boosting office-leasing activity in top tech hubs, CBRE reported. The firm’s 13th annual Scoring Tech Talent report highlights the clustering of AI jobs: 37% of AI jobs in the U.S. are found in the San Francisco Bay Area, New York City, Seattle and Washington, DC, while in Canada, the concentration is even greater as Toronto, Montreal and Vancouver claim 60% of AI jobs. CBRE expects the AI industry’s momentum to benefit office markets in key hubs. That’s especially true in San Francisco, where AI companies have accounted for 30% of leasing activity, roughly 10 million square feet, since 2023. “There’s no denying that AI is reshaping the tech industry and job growth in general,” said Colin Yasukochi, executive director of CBRE’s Tech Insights Center in San Francisco. “Growth of AI jobs in the U.S. far outpaced the broader tech-talent category, which expanded by 1.8% last year even as the tech industry cut some non-AI jobs. Markets adding AI jobs are further cementing their status as tech talent capitals.” The post CBRE: U.S. and Canadian AI Jobs Grow 45% Year-Over-Year appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: U.S. and Canadian AI jobs grew 45% YoY; AI roles now ~33% of tech listings.
37% of U.S. AI jobs in SF Bay, NYC, Seattle, DC; 60% of Canadian AI in Toronto, Montreal, Vancouver.
SF Bay AI companies drove ~10M SF office leasing since 2023; 30% of SF tech leasing.
stories.summary: CBRE's Tech Talent report found U.S. and Canadian AI employment surged 45% year-over-year, with AI roles comprising nearly one-third of U.S. tech job postings. 37% of U.S. AI jobs cluster in four metros (SF Bay, NYC, Seattle, DC), while in Canada the concentration is even tighter (60% in Toronto, Montreal, Vancouver). San Francisco's AI sector has driven roughly 10 million SF of office leasing since 2023.
stories.impact: Explosive AI job growth in top four U.S. metros (SF, NYC, Seattle, DC) and Canadian hubs signals sustained inbound talent migration and sustained office demand in those markets, which reinforces residential demand growth. For multifamily developers: prioritize supply expansion and site acquisition in and around FAANG and AI hotspots, especially secondary rings where land and construction costs are lower. NYC and DC multifamily will see continued pressure from tech talent influx; SF Bay supply constraints may persist. Seattle and secondary DC markets are undersupplied relative to job growth.

stories.title: PCCP, RPM Pick Up 358-Unit Arlington Multifamily Community
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between PCCP and RPM Living Investments has acquired Truman at Arlington Commons, a four-story multifamily community located at 505 E Lamar Boulevard in Arlington, TX. The property was developed and owned by The Nehemiah Company. Built in 2021, the property features 358 units with an average size of 807 square feet (sf), across floorplans ranging from 576 to 1,594 sf. The units feature 10-foot ceilings, with select units offering 14-foot ceiling heights. 4,900 square feet of ground-floor retail is occupied by Nehemiah Coffee Company. Truman at Arlington Commons is located in North Arlington, a centrally positioned pocket between Dallas and Fort Worth with direct access to Interstate 30. The location provides connectivity to Arlington’s primary employment and entertainment districts, including AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field, and Texas Live!, which together attract more than 50 million visitors annually. PCCP has approximately $29.3 billion in assets under management on behalf of institutional investors . The post PCCP, RPM Pick Up 358-Unit Arlington Multifamily Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: PCCP and RPM Living acquire Truman at Arlington Commons, TX; 358 units built 2021.
Average unit 807 SF; ground-floor retail (Nehemiah Coffee); I-30 access.
North Arlington location near AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field; 50M+ annual visitors.
stories.summary: A PCCP–RPM Living joint venture acquired Truman at Arlington Commons, a 358-unit, four-story multifamily community completed in 2021 and formerly held by The Nehemiah Company. Located in North Arlington with direct I-30 access and proximity to major employment and entertainment anchors (AT&T Stadium, Globe Life Field, Texas Live!), the property offers 4,900 SF of ground-floor retail occupied by Nehemiah Coffee Company.
stories.impact: Institutional investor acquisition of newly completed (3-year-old) multifamily in Arlington signals confidence in DFW metro demand and positive exit conditions. Arlington's central position between Dallas and Fort Worth, plus proximity to 50+ million annual visitors and stable employment anchors, supports rental fundamentals. For multifamily developers: this validates Arlington as a core DFW submarket for new supply; however, the property's recent vintage and quick institutional recap suggest limited value-add opportunity and strong existing competition. Focus on unmet demand or underserved submarkets in DFW rather than core Arlington.
